clue.text: Joke I finally see, told in old language

parts.note: a pun is a joke playing on words

indicators.note: told means spoken, so the word see is taken as it sounds when said

parts.note: the word see sounds like the letter C

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets a joke told in an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' only marks the last piece of the build. PUNIC is the language of ancient Carthage.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic was the Semitic tongue of ancient Carthage, long extinct.

clue.text: Ready for bed, arrange board underneath

indicators.note: underneath means the board piece goes below the other in this down clue

parts.note: to plan is to arrange in advance
a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Someone tired sets up a board below their bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is a flower bed, not where one sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plantable can be set into the soil of a garden plot.

clue.text: Shell liner in North American port

annotationWithheld.why: Shell liner in North American port (5): NACRE is N + ACRE, but Acre is a port in Israel, not America, so 'American' has no job in any parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Shell liner in North American port

clue.text: Whimsical author makes vehicle turn over

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A fanciful writer causes a car to overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll wrote the Alice books; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll wrote the nonsense classics Alice in Wonderland and Through the Looking-Glass.

clue.text: Hikes, using support groups

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
packs are groups, as of wolves or cards

explanation.surface: Someone goes on walks with help from organised parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpack is to go hiking carrying one's gear in a rucksack, so a person who backpacks hikes.

clue.text: Was very angry, yet kind of sweet

explanation.walkthrough: A boiled sweet is the British name for a hard candy.
explanation.definitionFit: To have boiled is to have raged; a boiled sweet is a hard candy made from boiled sugar.

clue.text: Container of cold wine tipped over

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: tipped over means upended, so the wine is read from bottom to top

parts.note: retsina is a resinated Greek wine

explanation.surface: A tin of chilled wine has been knocked onto its side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped over' turns RETSINA into ANISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round metal tin for holding tea, film or the like.

clue.text: One tries to remove batter from jug

definitions.meaning: the bowler in baseball, who aims to get the hitter out

explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like the kitchen mixture but is the baseball hitter.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the thrower tries to strike out the hitter; a pitcher is also a large jug.

clue.text: Pinch name held by two firms

indicators.note: held by means the name sits inside the other letters

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
strict is firm in the sense of stern

explanation.surface: A title is shared between a pair of businesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firms' gives two different words: a company noun, CO, and an adjective, STRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to squeeze or narrow something, as a pinch does.

clue.text: Playwright to give voice — listen!

indicators.note: listen tells the solver to go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: to sing is to give voice in song

explanation.surface: A dramatist demands attention for a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: J M Synge was an Irish dramatist, author of The Playboy of the Western World.
explanation.definitionFit: John Millington Synge wrote Irish plays such as Riders to the Sea.

clue.text: In a study, one's put on string instrument

indicators.note: In means the string-and-one pair sits inside the letters of 'a study'

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

indicators.note: put on means one piece is added after the other in this across clue

parts.note: a cord is a length of string
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone at a desk is busy restringing a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'string instrument' looks like one phrase, but string is wordplay and instrument alone is the definition. 'put on' sets the one after the string, and 'In' places that pair within 'a study'.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordion is a musical instrument played with bellows and keys or buttons.

clue.text: Saw result of one footballer being off?

definitions.text: Saw result of one footballer being off?

parts.words: Saw result of one footballer being off?
parts.note: a football side has eleven players, so with one sent off ten are on; the same letters name a joint piece cut with a saw

explanation.surface: A football fan watches a player get sent off and wonders what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenon is the projecting piece of a mortise-and-tenon joint, shaped with a tenon saw; read as two words it says ten (players) on (the pitch).
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the tongue cut by a saw on the end of a timber to fit a mortise.

clue.text: Authority that Hebrew poets misused

indicators.note: misused means wrongly handled, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An official body complains that Jewish poets have abused language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges the fifteen letters of THAT HEBREW POETS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names those holding power or official control, the establishment in charge.

clue.text: Fastening appears to give way

definitions.meaning: a clasp on a belt or shoe
to collapse or bend under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: A buckle is a clasp for a strap, and to buckle is to crumple or collapse under strain.

clue.text: Fried dish made from game — the outer parts only

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops

indicators.note: outer parts only means keep just the first and last letters of the word the

explanation.surface: A fritter made from game meat uses only the outside bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like hunted meat but is the lawn game; the outer letters of THE are T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small roll of minced food coated in breadcrumbs and deep-fried.

clue.text: Money-making knowledge

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, the British unit of money
earning is making money, as in making a living

explanation.surface: Knowing how to get rich is a skill in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money-making' reads as one adjective, but it splits into two pieces: L and EARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is acquired knowledge or scholarship, as in a person of great learning.

clue.text: Plant found under logs, going wild

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weed is spotted growing out of control beneath some timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link; 'going wild' rearranges UNDER LOGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common yellow-flowered weed of gardens and waste ground.

clue.text: Emphatic sort of type, showing impudence

definitions.meaning: heavy printing letters used for emphasis

explanation.definitionFit: Heavy printed lettering is used for stress; a bold face is also a brazen, cheeky manner.

clue.text: School whip used to distress girls, so to speak

definitions.text: used to distress girls, so to speak

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
a crop is a short riding whip

explanation.surface: A school caning implement was used to upset female pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' is read as dis-tress, taking the tresses away; an Eton crop is a very short, boyish women's haircut of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eton crop was a closely cut hairstyle worn by women, removing their long hair.

clue.text: Cook ached to get discharge from cell here

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify them, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone cooking in prison aches to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' is an electric battery cell, not a prison; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In a battery the electrode from which current flows out into the circuit is this one.

clue.text: Take diplomat in fancy car to inner city area

indicators.note: in means the diplomat is placed inside the car's letters

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a high-performance touring car
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone drives an envoy in a smart car into a deprived urban district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is a link here, telling the solver to assemble the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a poor, densely populated district of a city, often occupied by a minority group.

clue.text: Raises call for surrender

definitions.meaning: lifts the arms, as when volunteering
the order given by an armed captor

explanation.definitionFit: Lifting arms in a vote is a show of this; it is also the demand shouted to someone being captured.

clue.text: Graduate, upset — said to be unprincipled

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in this down clue the letters are read upwards

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A distressed graduate is described as lacking scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an adjective for the graduate but turns MA into AM; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking any moral sense or principles at all.

clue.text: Quarter to one, mind, is wrong time

parts.note: a quarter is one fourth of something

indicators.note: wrong means not in proper order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes the clock reads quarter to one and is told they are mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ONE MIND IS into DIMENSION; 'to' is a link joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, time is treated as an extra coordinate beyond the three of space.

clue.text: Tired US official's rebellious

parts.note: a Fed is an American federal agent, as of the FBI
up means in revolt, as in up in arms

explanation.surface: A weary American official has turned to revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'official's' joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fed up means being tired of and bored by something.

clue.text: It describes the investment of a decade

definitions.text: It describes the investment of a decade

parts.words: It describes the investment of a decade
parts.note: investment is the old military sense of besieging; the epic tells of the ten-year siege of Troy

explanation.surface: A financial report covers ten years of putting money into shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' looks financial, but means a siege, the act of surrounding a city with troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem recounts part of the Greek siege of Troy, which lasted ten years.

clue.text: Make do by shortening this

parts.note: the two-letter form do is a written short form of a word meaning the same again

explanation.surface: Someone is told to improvise by cutting this down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make do' looks like the idiom for managing, but it means produce the word do; the abbreviation do is used in lists for the word meaning as above.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the same thing again, and is abbreviated to do in lists.

clue.text: Taken down, these lines begin to make extra sense

definitions.text: Taken down, these lines begin to make extra sense

parts.words: Taken down, these lines begin to make extra sense
parts.note: the first letters of each line of verse, read downwards, spell out a further word or message

explanation.surface: A note copied out begins to make more sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken down' looks like writing something out, but it means read from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: These are poems or puzzles where the initial letters of successive lines spell a hidden word.

clue.text: Reported agreement to introduce planned fare gradually

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: peace is an agreement ending a war
a meal is a set serving of food prepared in advance

explanation.surface: A deal is said to bring in a scheduled menu bit by bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to introduce' is a link joining the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done in stages, little by little.

clue.text: This controller can get depressed by Oxford

definitions.text: This controller can get depressed by Oxford

parts.words: This controller can get depressed by Oxford
parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced shoe, so the control is one pressed down by a shod foot

explanation.surface: A university official is said to be getting gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university, but an Oxford is a lace-up shoe; 'depressed' means pushed down, not sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-operated lever, as on a bike, car or piano, is pushed down by the shoe.
